- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 92+), then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts too long after peaks.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops; underreacts to downward momentum.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 10 days, then too pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggests asymmetric horizon bias.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility clustering — over-smooths transitions between high and low zones.
- When history includes a recent sharp decline, model fails to adjust downward quickly — underestimates risk of further drop.
- Forecasts often ignore the influence of recent low prices — fails to “anchor” to recent minima.
- Model tends to overfit to recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation even after price correction.
- Forecasts show a “tail risk” bias — underestimate the probability of extreme low prices after a spike.
